subject: Pricing for augmenting new teams & commit-tier options
messages:
From: Elena Stanton <elena.stanton@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Expanding Redwood usage — pricing question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with latency and the KV caching behavior. We’re planning to start a second pilot that would add two new internal products on top of the initial chatbot workload. Ballpark estimate is an incremental ~250M tokens/month across the two products by Q4.

Before we move legal/procurement, can you confirm:
- Whether incremental tokens under hosted API can be covered by our existing commit or need a separate tier;
- Typical per-token discount thresholds at the 250M and 1B/month marks; and
- Any minimum time commitments for an add-on team to inherit the same pricing?

We’ll likely need a clear path for staged commits (pilot -> QA -> prod) and an estimate of any one-time migration/onboarding credits you might offer.

Appreciate the quick callout — looping in procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) for visibility.

Best,
Elena
Elena Stanton
Director of Product — Consumer Health
Acme Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Stanton <elena.stanton@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expanding Redwood usage — pricing question

Elena — thanks for the context and the heads-up to procurement. Great to hear the demo landed well. Short answers up-front, then a proposed approach: 

1) Incremental tokens and commit handling
- We can either fold incremental token usage into your existing commit (preferred for simplicity) or create a supplemental commit for the new teams. Folding into the existing commit is cleaner if you expect combined usage to be steady; supplemental commits are helpful for isolated billing/teams.

2) Discount thresholds (hosted API, per-token) — current guidance
- < 100M/mo: standard list pricing
- 100M–499M/mo: 10% volume discount on per-token rate (applies to tokens over the threshold)
- 500M–999M/mo: 18% volume discount
- >=1B/mo: 25% volume discount + eligibility for enterprise rate card (further negotiation)

3) Minimum time commitments for add-on teams
- No obligator y multi-year requirement to add a team. For folded-into-existing-commit we recommend a 6-month forecast window and a 3-month billing cadence. For a supplemental commit tier we usually request a 12-month commit for predictable capacity with a 30–60 day ramping allowance.

Proposed staged approach (what I suggest for Acme):
- Phase 1 (Pilot, 1–2 months): add the two products under the existing commit; Redwood applies a pilot credit equal to 10% of projected incremental usage for the first month (one-time).
- Phase 2 (QA, months 3–4): if usage grows to >200M/mo, convert to a supplemental commit for those teams (6–12 month length, customer preference).
- Phase 3 (Prod, month 5+): once sustained >=500M combined we apply the 18% band to the applicable tokens and revisit enterprise pricing if you expect to cross 1B.

I attached a draft pricing worksheet with numbers rolled up into three scenarios (pilot, steady-state 300M, steady-state 800M) and a short commit/SLA draft for procurement. See attachments: redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.xlsx, commit-sla-draft.pdf

Next steps: if that aligns, Marissa (cc’d) can put together a short commercial term sheet and I can schedule a 30-min procurement review with our finance & CSX folks.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Stanton <elena.stanton@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expanding Redwood usage — pricing question

Karthik — this is very helpful, thank you. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 250M number is our Q4 conservative guess; if the pilot converts we could see a 450–600M run rate across the two products within six months.
- We prefer to keep billing scoped per team for chargeback to product owners; procurement will push back on folding everything into the existing commit unless there’s a clear cost-savings.
- Two procurement asks: (a) can you give a sample term sheet showing split commits (team A vs team B) and blended discount impact? (b) what specific observability credits or extended logs retention do you include for committed customers?

If you can provide the split-commit term sheet and a short explanation of retention/observability add-ons, procurement will evaluate and push to legal.

Best,
Elena

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Stanton <elena.stanton@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expanding Redwood usage — pricing question

Elena / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a revised worksheet showing two split-commit examples (Scenario A: Team A 300M, Team B 200M; Scenario B: Team A 450M, Team B 150M) and the blended per-token effective rate including the tiered discounts. Key callouts: 
- Blended pricing: we apply tiered discounts at the aggregate account level but can invoice separately per commit (so chargeback works while discount bands are evaluated on total usage unless you elect per-commit-only bands).
- Migration/onboarding credits: one-time pilot credit (10% of incremental tokens for month 1) + up to $5k onboarding credits for engineering integration if you sign within 30 days.
- Observability & retention: committed customers get 90 days of extended request-level tracing by default; longer retention (180/365 days) is available as an add-on at fixed monthly rates — I listed the options in the worksheet. We can also include an SLA for trace preservation in the 12-month commit.

Commercial next steps: Marissa will prepare the split-commit term sheet and a short pricing appendix. If procurement approves, I’ll open a commercial worksheet in DocuSign for signatures and route to our finance team to finalize the commit.

Proposed times to hop on a 30-min call with finance & procurement: Fri 7/17 9:00–9:30am PT or Mon 7/20 11:00–11:30am PT. Which works for you?

Thanks —
Karthik

Attachments: redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.xlsx (pricing scenarios), commit-sla-draft.pdf (SLA + onboarding credits)
